newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil 97 current account gap seen at 4.5 pct/GDP.
newsitem.headline: Brazil 97 current account gap seen at 4.5 pct/GDP.

text.p: Brazil's balance of payments current account gap is expected to widen to about 4.5 percent of gross domestic product by the end of the year, said a senior Central Bank official Monday.
Altamir Lopes, head of the bank's economics department, said the figure was by no means a "target" but based on current trends.
"This is not a target but the data available allows you to predict a deficit (in the current account) of about 4.5 percent (of GDP)," Lopes told reporters.
The current account deficit in the 12 months to June reached 4.19 percent of GDP, a touch wider than the 4.07 percent gap posted in the 12 months to May.
"The tendency is for it to widen a bit more," Lopes said.
Brazil ended 1996 with a current account deficit equivalent to 3.25 percent of GDP.
